case_studies.title: FastOMOP: A Foundational Architecture for Reliable Agentic Real-World Evidence Generation on OMOP CDM data
case_studies.abstract: The Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model (OMOP CDM), maintained by the Observational Health Data Sciences and Informatics (OHDSI) collaboration, enabled the harmonisation of electronic health records data of nearly one billion patients in 83 countries. Yet generating real-world evidence (RWE) from these repositories remains a manual process requiring clinical, epidemiological and technical expertise. case_studies.summary: The Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model (OMOP CDM) has harmonized electronic health records data of nearly one billion patients, but generating real-world evidence from these repositories remains a manual process. The proposed FastOMOP architecture utilizes AI agents and Large Language Models (LLMs) to automate the process of generating real-world evidence. The outcome of this approach is the potential to increase efficiency and reduce the need for manual expertise in clinical and epidemiological tasks.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can leverage the OMOP CDM to develop and train AI models that can automate the process of generating real-world evidence. By utilizing AI agents and LLMs, practitioners can create more efficient and scalable solutions for real-world evidence generation.
case_studies.monetisation: The FastOMOP architecture presents a clear product opportunity for companies looking to develop automated solutions for real-world evidence generation. By commercializing this technology, companies can offer valuable services to healthcare organizations and pharmaceutical companies, enabling them to make more informed decisions with data-driven insights.

case_studies.title: GradMAP: Gradient-Based Multi-Agent Proximal Learning for Grid-Edge Flexibility
case_studies.abstract: Coordinating large populations of grid-edge devices requires learning methods that remain fully decentralised in deployment while still respecting three-phase AC distribution-network physics. This paper proposes gradient-based multi-agent proximal learning (GradMAP) to address this challenge. GradMAP trains independent neural-network policies for each agent without any parameter sharing, and each agent uses only its own local observation for online decision-making without communication. case_studies.summary: The problem of coordinating large populations of grid-edge devices is addressed through a decentralized learning approach. The proposed GradMAP method uses gradient-based multi-agent proximal learning to train independent neural-network policies for each agent. This approach enables online decision-making without communication, respecting three-phase AC distribution-network physics.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can utilize gradient-based methods to train decentralized agents, allowing for efficient decision-making in complex systems. By embedding differentiable power-flow models, practitioners can ensure that their solutions respect the underlying physics of the system.
case_studies.monetisation: The GradMAP method presents a clear opportunity for product development in the energy sector, particularly in the management of grid-edge devices. A company could leverage this approach to create a decentralized energy management system, offering a competitive solution for utilities and grid operators.

case_studies.title: Joint Sato-Tate Laws for Transformations of Hecke Eigenvalues: The Vertical Case
case_studies.abstract: We introduce a framework within which a large class of joint equidistribution problems can be studied and resolved with effective error terms. This involves proving a higher dimensional and $μ$-analogue of the Erdös-Turán inequality, and utilizing the theory of the Hardy-Krause (H-K) variation from analysis, where, in particular, we formulate a technique to approximate a broad class of relevant functions by functions of bounded H-K variation. Our main focus will be on the vertical Sato-Tate problem for spaces of cusp forms and for families of elliptic curves over finite fields. In particular,
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed is the joint equidistribution of Hecke eigenvalues, which is a complex mathematical concept. The AI approach involves utilizing the theory of the Hardy-Krause variation and formulating a technique to approximate relevant functions. The outcome is a framework for studying and resolving joint equidistribution problems with effective error terms.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this concept to other problems, AI practitioners can utilize the theory of the Hardy-Krause variation and develop techniques to approximate relevant functions. This can be achieved by formulating a framework to study and resolve complex mathematical problems with effective error terms.
case_studies.monetisation: The monetisation potential of this concept is limited as it is a purely academic concept, but it can be adapted into a product or service that provides mathematical solutions to complex problems. A potential business opportunity could be to develop a software or tool that utilizes the Hardy-Krause variation to solve mathematical problems in various fields.

case_studies.title: Learning to Think from Multiple Thinkers
case_studies.abstract: We study learning with Chain-of-Thought (CoT) supervision from multiple thinkers, all of whom provide correct but possibly systematically different solutions, e.g., step-by-step solutions to math problems written by different thinkers, or step-by-step execution traces of different programs solving the same problem. We consider classes that are computationally easy to learn using CoT supervision from a single thinker, but hard to learn with only end-result supervision, i.e., without CoT (Joshi et al. 2025). We establish that, under cryptographic assumptions, learning can be hard from CoT superv
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this study is the challenge of learning from Chain-of-Thought (CoT) supervision from multiple thinkers, which can provide systematically different solutions to the same problem. The AI approach involves analyzing the feasibility of learning with CoT supervision from multiple thinkers and establishing the hardness of learning under cryptographic assumptions. The outcome of this study provides insights into the limitations of CoT supervision and its potential applications in various domains.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply the findings of this study, AI practitioners should consider the potential biases and limitations of CoT supervision from multiple thinkers when designing learning models. By understanding the hardness of learning from CoT supervision, practitioners can develop more effective and robust learning strategies that account for the variability in human thinking.
case_studies.monetisation: The study's findings have potential applications in areas such as education and workforce training, where personalized learning models can be developed to account for individual differences in thinking and problem-solving. A concrete business opportunity arising from this research could be the development of AI-powered adaptive learning platforms that incorporate CoT supervision from multiple thinkers to provide more effective and personalized learning experiences.

case_studies.title: Green Shielding: A User-Centric Approach Towards Trustworthy AI
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed, yet their outputs can be highly sensitive to routine, non-adversarial variation in how users phrase queries, a gap not well addressed by existing red-teaming efforts. We propose Green Shielding, a user-centric agenda for building evidence-backed deployment guidance by characterizing how benign input variation shifts model behavior. We operationalize this agenda through the CUE criteria: benchmarks with authentic Context, reference standards and metrics that capture true Utility, and perturbations that reflect realistic variations in the E
case_studies.summary: The problem of large language models being sensitive to variations in user queries is addressed in this study. The proposed AI approach, Green Shielding, aims to characterize how benign input variation shifts model behavior through the CUE criteria. The outcome is a user-centric agenda for building evidence-backed deployment guidance, contributing to more trustworthy AI systems.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply the Green Shielding approach, AI practitioners should focus on characterizing the impact of realistic input variations on model behavior, using benchmarks with authentic context and reference standards. By doing so, they can develop more robust and user-centric AI systems that are less sensitive to routine query variations.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity arising from this research is the development of AI-powered tools that can automatically assess and improve the robustness of large language models, offering a competitive advantage to companies deploying these models. Such tools could be marketed as a service to AI developers and organizations, providing a concrete monetization opportunity for the Green Shielding approach.
